Q: What is the Fundamental Vow Dharma?

A: When Amitabha Buddha in former times was the monk Dharmakara, he made forty-eight great vows to bring about the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss in order to save all sentient beings. The eighteenth of these is called Amitabha’s Fundamental Vow. The eighteenth vow is:

“If, when I attain Buddhahood, sentient beings in the ten directions, with sincere mind and joyful faith, should wish to be reborn in my land, and if even ten thoughts [of recitation] should not bring about their rebirth, may I not attain the right enlightenment. Only excluding those who commit the five heinous offenses and slander the right Dharma.”
(See the Sutra of the Buddha Speaks of the Immeasurable Life Buddha.)
The
“even ten thoughts” spoken of in this eighteenth vow
refers to ten continuous thoughts at the moment of death
. For its detailed basis, see the article
“The Eighteenth Vow”
As for how
one can be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss
, Master Shandao, who is the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha, has made it perfectly clear
(for details, see the article
“Master Shandao’s Pure Land Teaching”
Precisely because reciting the name is easy,
continuous thought brings rebirth
. If one can
be mindful thought after thought without interruption
making the end of one’s life the limit
, then
out of ten, ten are reborn; out of a hundred, a hundred are reborn.
May all people reflect well and, whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down, must
rouse their minds and restrain themselves
not ceasing day or night
; with the previous thought ending at death, the next thought immediately brings rebirth.
Ever enjoying the unconditioned bliss of the Dharma, up to the attainment of Buddhahood — how joyful is that!
[Continuous thought brings rebirth]
At the moment of death, the thought of Buddha-recitation being continuous
(not interrupted by deluded thoughts)
, one is then reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.

Here “continuous” means the thought of Buddha-recitation, thought after thought succeeding without any deluded thought mixed in (if a deluded thought is mixed in, it is no longer continuous). “Be mindful thought after thought, making the end of life the limit” means to keep this continuity of thought until it becomes second nature, so as to guarantee the ten continuous thoughts at the moment of death.
The ten continuous thoughts at the moment of death — this is the condition for rebirth.
(For details, see the article
“The Condition for Rebirth: Ten Continuous Thoughts at the Moment of Death”

[Rouse the mind and restrain oneself] “Rousing the mind” means to stir up one’s mind to do what should be done; “restraining oneself” means to restrain oneself from doing what should not be done. These four characters are a powerful weapon for overcoming difficulties and clearing away obstacles.
[Not ceasing day or night] Do not stop the thought-after-thought continuity either day or night.

[With the previous thought ending at death, the next thought immediately brings rebirth] This means: because the thought of Buddha-recitation is continuous, the last thought at the moment of death is necessarily a thought of Buddha-recitation,
and immediately after that last thought
one is reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Master Shandao is the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha; his words are the words of Amitabha Buddha. As for how one may be reborn, surely his words are the authority!

The distinguishing feature of the Fundamental Vow Dharma is that it twists the “even ten thoughts” of the eighteenth vow into meaning reciting Amitabha’s name ten times in daily life with a distracted mind. Hence they proclaim “the name being recited brings certain rebirth” (so long as one recites the Buddha’s name a little in ordinary life, at death one is certain to be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss), and for this reason one need not cultivate, need not observe the precepts, need not do good, need not purify one’s own mind — indeed, even doing evil for a whole life is of no consequence, because “the evil person is the true subject of Amitabha Buddha’s salvation”, and this is Amitabha’s Fundamental Vow. For example, Master Huijing says in The Essential Meaning of Master Shandao:
“The purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to reveal the Fundamental Vow of Amitabha: the evil person is the true subject.”
Master Honen said:
“If a person commits the five heinous offenses

(the five heinous offenses: five kinds of crimes utterly contrary to reason, namely killing one’s father, killing one’s mother, killing an arhat, drawing blood from a Buddha’s body, and breaking the harmony of the Sangha. These five are acts of extreme evil; committing any one of them causes one to fall into the uninterrupted hell, hence they are also called the ‘uninterrupted karma’)
, and hears the name of six syllables
(hears ‘Namo Amitabha Buddha’)
, the chariot of fire naturally departs
(the fiery chariot of hell naturally departs)
, and the lotus seat comes to welcome him.”
(recorded from the Forty-Eight Sayings of Master Honen, compiled by Master Huijing, also titled the Comforting Words on Buddha-Recitation; for its errors see
“Master Honen’s Comforting Words on Buddha-Recitation”

) This says that a great evil person who has committed the five heinous offenses, merely upon hearing the Buddha’s name, is reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss to enjoy forever all happiness. If this were really so, what evil deed in the world would anyone still dare not to commit?
This is utterly inverted teaching!
For the refutation of these fallacies, see
“The Fundamental Vow Dharma Is a Non-Buddhist School Attached to Buddhism”
, appendix nine: “Refuting ‘Reciting the Name Brings Certain Rebirth’ and the ‘Evil Person as True Subject’ Theory”
“Reciting the name brings certain rebirth”
and
“the evil person as the true subject”
these two points are the
heart-essence
of the Fundamental Vow Dharma.
It cleverly exploits human weaknesses — fear of difficulty, love of shortcuts, and craving for worldly pleasures — to trick believers.

“Reciting the name brings certain rebirth” is the theoretical basis for renunciants not needing to cultivate, and “the evil person as the true subject” is the theoretical basis for renunciants not needing to observe the precepts or to cease evil and do good. Thus renunciants degenerate from cultivators of the Way into professional monks who neither observe the precepts nor cultivate; growing hair, eating meat, taking wives, doing evil, and so on — anything goes. Sadly, they still think they will certainly be reborn, because they have these two guarantees — “reciting the name brings certain rebirth” and “the evil person as the true subject” — not realizing these are all deceitful lies! See
“The Fundamental Vow Dharma Is a Non-Buddhist School Attached to Buddhism”
and
“The Practice of Master Honen’s Teaching”
“Reciting the name brings certain rebirth” and “the evil person as the true subject”
these two points are the heart-essence of the Fundamental Vow Dharma] This is spoken personally by Master Honen. Honen said: “The
heart-essence
of the Pure Land school lies in this: whoever it may be, if one recites the Buddha’s name, one is reborn.
Even an evil person the like of whom
(nothing can compare with)
cannot be found in the world
, if he recites Namo Amitabha Buddha,
even with a single thought he is reborn
(excerpted from the Forty-Eight Sayings of Master Honen, compiled by Master Huijing, also titled the Comforting Words on Buddha-Recitation
for details see
“A Critique of the Comforting Words on Buddha-Recitation”

Originally, the Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma and the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma came from the same source: their theories both derive from Master Honen and Master Shinran, and the content they proclaim is likewise the same (only the Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma is better at concealing it, not so naked). But because the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma founded by Master Honen and Master Shinran has such a bad name, Master Huijing of the so-called “Pure Land school” in Taiwan and Master Jingzong of Hongyuan Temple in mainland China attempt to deceive our believers by changing their facade. Master Huijing says: “So our school is not some Japanese Pure Land (school),
our Fundamental Vow Dharma

is the school of Amitabha Buddha’s eighteenth vow.” (See “Master Huijing: What Is the Transmission of the Fundamental Vow Dharma?”) In this way, the Fundamental Vow Dharma now has a distinction between the Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma and the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma, though it is only changing the soup without changing the medicine.
[The so-called “Pure Land school”]

The term “Pure Land school” originally refers to the school among the ten schools of Buddhism that practices exclusively Buddha-recitation seeking rebirth in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, with Master Huiyuan of the Jin dynasty as its first patriarch.
For a thousand years this has been a great school standing alongside the Chan school

. Yet that Fundamental Vow Dharma of theirs is merely a small sect, and Master Huijing actually names it the “Pure Land school”, as if they were the whole Pure Land school! This is deliberately creating confusion, mixing fish eyes with pearls to pass off the false as the true, in order to deceive people who do not know the truth, especially beginning Buddhists, leading them to mistake them for the Pure Land school and board their pirate ship. — This is the very means by which the Fundamental Vow Dharma lives:
deceit!
Followers of the Buddha must sharpen their eyes,
and whenever they encounter a group or website that names itself the “Pure Land school”, they must carefully discern whether it is the Fundamental Vow Dharma, so as not to be deceived

. The method of discernment is also simple: if it is led by Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and the like, proclaiming the views and theories of the Fundamental Vow Dharma — for example, the Pure Land school Hongyuan Temple, the Pure Land school
Pure Land school portal
Chinese Pure Land school

Global Pure Land school portal website, the Chinese Pure Land school Association, and so on — then it is the Fundamental Vow Dharma of a non-Buddhist school attached to Buddhism, not the true Pure Land school.
Their real names should be: the Fundamental Vow Dharma Hongyuan Temple, the Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma
global portal website, the Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma Association, and so on; only then would the name match the reality

[The ten schools] The Kosa school, the Satyasiddhi school, the Chan school, the Tiantai school, the Huayan school, the Shingon school, the Dharmalaksana school, the Pure Land school, the Vinaya school, and the Sanlun school. [The views and theories of the Fundamental Vow Dharma] See
“The Fundamental Vow Dharma Is a Non-Buddhist School Attached to Buddhism”
As for the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma, see
“The Practice of Master Honen’s Teaching”
“Do Not Promote the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma”
“The Fundamental Vow Dharma Is a Non-Buddhist School Attached to Buddhism”

and other writings. As for the Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma, they no longer dare to fly the banner of Master Honen and Master Shinran, so they fly the banner of “relying on Master Shandao” to peddle “reciting the name brings certain rebirth” and “
the evil person as the true subject theory
”. In fact, what they say and what they do is genuinely opposed to Master Shandao; see
“Honen and Others Distort and Slander Master Shandao”

. And this “Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma” likewise twists the “even ten thoughts” of the eighteenth vow into meaning ten thoughts in daily life; likewise it proclaims: reciting the name brings certain rebirth, no need to observe the precepts, no need to cultivate merit, no need to purify one’s own mind, even doing evil for a whole life is of no consequence, because “the evil person is the true subject of Amitabha Buddha’s salvation”. (See Master Jinghui’s The Essential Meaning of the Pure Land School, and Master Jingzong’s Master Shandao’s Pure Land Thought, Master Jingzong’s Buddha-Gate Internet Interview, and other books and talks.) As for the “three countries, seven patriarchs” (
the bodhisattvas Nagarjuna and Vasubandhu of India, and Master Tanluan, Master Daochuo, Master Shandao of China, and Master Genshin and Master Honen of Japan

), “discarding the Essential Gate and establishing the Vow Gate” (discarding the Essential Gate, establishing the Vow Gate), “his doing, my receiving” (the matter of rebirth Amitabha Buddha has already accomplished for me; I need only believe), the denial of karmic retribution (all the evil I have done is borne by Amitabha Buddha on my behalf), the denial of “self-done, self-received” (no matter what evil one does, so long as one believes in Amitabha’s Fundamental Vow, Amitabha Buddha will certainly bear it for me, without the least effect on rebirth), and the evil-person-as-true-subject theory (Amitabha Buddha’s salvation takes the evil person as its true subject), and so on — which of these does not originate from the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma? Even the trick of flying the banner “relying on Master Shandao” to deceive believers was picked up from Master Honen and Master Shinran. Moreover, in the preface to the Collected Passages on Rebirth from the Three Pure Land Sutras, translated by Master Huijing and written by Shinran,
he boasts of the teachings of Honen and Shinran’s Fundamental Vow Dharma (the Jodo Shinshu) as the pinnacle thought of the Pure Land school

, and claims “if one is ignorant and does not learn, one loses the great benefit of rebirth”. Master Huijing’s followers then exalt Shinran’s Collected Passages on Rebirth from the Three Pure Land Sutras as “the Light of the Land of Ultimate Bliss”.

Let me also mention here the connection of Master Huijing and Master Jingzong with the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma. In the spring of 1985, Master Huijing of Taiwan went alone to the mountains for quiet cultivation, which lasted three years. During this time he read Master Honen’s Collection of Passages on the Selection of the Nembutsu of the Fundamental Vow,
“and realized that the Pure Land teaching should take the Shandao stream
(the so-called “Shandao stream” is the teaching system of Master Honen; Master Shinran, Honen’s disciple, established the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma according to this teaching system)

as the most pure and correct: above, it accords with Amitabha’s fundamental intent to save beings; below, it accords with the capacities of all sentient beings. In the autumn of 1988 he studied abroad at Otani University in Kyoto, Japan
(Otani University is a private university established by the Japanese Jodo Shinshu, that is, the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma)
, where he studied the Shandao-lineage Pure Land thought
(the “Shandao-lineage Pure Land thought” is the alias of the “Shinshu studies” of the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma; “Shinshu studies” is the foremost course at Otani University)
(the above is recorded from their own self-written A Brief Biography of Master Huijing) Master Xinyuan, a disciple of Master Huijing, also wrote in his open letter replying to Master Jingzong: “
To speak truthfully, we
(that is, Master Xinyuan, Master Jingzong, and others)
have also received the grace of the Shinshu teaching. Our study of the Fundamental Vow originates from our teacher
(Master Huijing)
, and our teacher studied it in Japan, immersing himself in Shinshu for three years.

[Editor’s note: This passage makes perfectly clear the lineage between the Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma led by Master Huijing and the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma with Honen and Shinran as its patriarchs.]

Thus Master Huijing personally went to the private university of the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma to “seek the Way”, and received his teaching lineage from the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma (see also his book The Essential Meaning of the Pure Land School, written after he returned from Japan). In 1996, Master Jingzong of mainland China took refuge with Master Huijing and vigorously promoted the Fundamental Vow Dharma throughout the mainland (which they euphemistically call “vigorously propagating Master Shandao’s Buddha-recitation Dharma in the mainland”), spreading it to every province.

Interestingly, the Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma led by Master Huijing actually received its lineage from the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma, taking Honen and Shinran as its patriarchs, yet everywhere it insists on “drawing a clear line” between itself and the Japanese Fundamental Vow Dharma and Honen and Shinran — this may be called betraying one’s teacher and destroying one’s ancestors. From this, its falsity is all the more evident!

[Editor’s note: Because the name “Fundamental Vow Dharma” has such a bad reputation, the Chinese Fundamental Vow Dharma led by Master Huijing does not dare to use it openly, and often substitutes “relying on Master Shandao”, “propagating Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought”, “propagating Master Shandao’s Buddha-recitation Dharma”
. Yet Master Shandao gave three extremely important teachings: first, single-minded Buddha-recitation; second, continuous thought brings rebirth; third, right mindfulness at the moment of death.
(See
“Master Shandao’s Pure Land Teaching”
article
In these three teachings, Master Shandao gave a clear exposition of how one can be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss.
This is
the Pure Land teaching of Master Shandao, the manifestation of Amitabha Buddha
. Yet in the “Master Shandao’s sayings” compiled by Master Huijing and Master Jingzong
(see The Collected Works of Master Shandao, compiled by Master Huijing and Master Jingzong and published in 2005 by the Pure Land School Publishing House)
they
dare not include it

, for fear of exposing their true colors. This fully proves that their reliance on Master Shandao is false, and that they are peddling their own goods under the banner of “reliance”; it also fully proves that the “Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought” they propagate is not the true Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought, but one they have manufactured from their own private goods — just watch the video Master Shandao’s Pure Land Thought
(lectured by Master Jingzong in 2006)
and you will know.
In Master Jingzong’s lecture series of forty-three long episodes
Master Shandao’s Pure Land Thought
, going on and on, he keeps saying that
the “Vow Gate” and “reciting the name brings certain rebirth” are the core of Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought. But what are the facts? The facts are:
Master Shandao never spoke of the Vow Gate; this was wholly fabricated by Master Honen
(see
“Master Honen Fabricated the Vow Gate”
article)
. Master Shandao also never said reciting the name brings certain rebirth; quite the contrary, Master Shandao said: continuous thought brings rebirth
(see
“Master Shandao’s Pure Land Teaching”
article)

The “Vow Gate” and “reciting the name brings certain rebirth” that they themselves fabricated are forcibly attributed to Master Shandao, falsely claiming this is Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought. Is this how one propagates Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought?

These three teachings of Master Shandao (“the primary and auxiliary practices”, “continuous thought brings rebirth”, and “right mindfulness at the moment of death”) are a demon-revealing mirror. Set the words of Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and the like against them, and whether they rely on Master Shandao, whether they propagate Master Shandao’s Pure Land thought, whether they propagate Master Shandao’s Buddha-recitation Dharma — whether true or false, whether right or wrong — is at once plainly seen.]
Q: Is the Fundamental Vow Dharma a non-Buddhist school attached to Buddhism?

A: The Fundamental Vow Dharma is of course a non-Buddhist school attached to Buddhism. What is called a non-Buddhist school attached to Buddhism is one that fastens itself to Buddhism while distorting and tampering with Buddhist doctrine.
The Fundamental Vow Dharma fully fits this definition, so it is a genuine non-Buddhist school attached to Buddhism.
An ordinary non-Buddhist school attached to Buddhism flies the banner of Buddhism to fool the people in order to win fame and profit, or even to achieve some political goal.
But the Fundamental Vow Dharma goes far beyond this:
it aims to destroy the right Dharma of the Buddha from the very root
. So, besides having systematic false teachings to distort and tamper with Buddhist doctrine, it also instigates the breaking of precepts and the doing of evil in order to destroy the Sangha.

(The Fundamental Vow Dharma holds that monks may take wives and eat meat; its scripture The Purpose of the Shinshu Teaching says: “Though the sins of ordinary beings are great, compared with the power of the vow they are but a single drop in the ocean, so it matters not whether one eats meat or keeps a wife.” Huijing and others vigorously proclaim: no need to cultivate, no need to observe the precepts, no need to do good, no need to purify one’s own mind, even doing evil for a whole life is of no consequence, the evil person is the true subject of Amitabha Buddha’s salvation. Master Huijing says: “The purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to reveal the Fundamental Vow of Amitabha: the evil person is the true subject. ... The Fundamental Vow Dharma is the evil person as the true subject.” Master Xinyuan, Huijing’s refuge disciple, says: “Let us now look at what kind of sentient being Amitabha Buddha’s salvation takes as its true subject? The evil person as the true subject.”)
And through the so-called “threefold discarding and establishing” (see
“The Fundamental Vow Dharma Is a Non-Buddhist School Attached to Buddhism”
article
it destroys the right Dharma by exterminating those who differ from it.
This is where the enormous harmfulness of the Fundamental Vow Dharma lies!

Q: The Contemplation Sutra of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life says that even people who commit the five heinous offenses and the ten evil deeds can also be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss. Therefore, reciting the name brings certain rebirth.
A: In the Contemplation Sutra of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life, those who commit the five heinous offenses and the ten evil deeds are not reborn simply by reciting the name,
but rather by accomplishing the ten continuous thoughts at the moment of death and extinguishing their offenses to gain rebirth
(see
“Annotated Notes on the Lowest-Lowest Birth Chapter of the Contemplation Sutra”

Originally, the “lowest-lowest birth chapter of the Contemplation Sutra” speaks of the grade of a person who is reborn in this way (a person who, having accomplished the ten continuous thoughts at the moment of death and extinguished offenses, is reborn) as the lowest-lowest grade.
Yet the Fundamental Vow Dharma deliberately omits
the ten continuous thoughts at the moment of death

this key point, exaggerating it into all those who commit the five heinous offenses and the ten evil deeds being reborn, and so proclaims “reciting the name brings certain rebirth” and the so-called evil-person-as-true-subject theory. (Master Huijing’s The Essential Meaning of Master Shandao says: “The purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to reveal the Fundamental Vow of Amitabha, the evil person as the true subject.” Master Xinyuan, Huijing’s refuge disciple, says: “Let us now look at what kind of sentient being Amitabha Buddha’s salvation takes as its true subject? The evil person as the true subject.”) Our original teacher, Shakyamuni Buddha, declared with his golden mouth that the
Sutra Praising the Pure Land of the Buddha’s Reception
, praised and received by Amitabha Buddha of the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, says:
“Sentient beings of little wholesome roots cannot attain rebirth in the pure Buddha-land of Ultimate Bliss of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life.”
In the Sutra of the Buddha Speaks of Amitabha, the Buddha says:
“Sariputra! One cannot, with little wholesome roots, merits, and conditions
(cannot, with the conditions of little wholesome roots and merits)
, be reborn in that land
(the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss)
Yet the Fundamental Vow Dharma vigorously proclaims “the evil person as the true subject” — its slandering of the Buddha and destruction of the Dharma reaches such a point!

Weigh for yourself: those who neither diligently and single-mindedly recite the Buddha’s name, nor observe the precepts, nor cultivate merit, nor purify their own mind, and even do evil for a whole life (including slandering the right Dharma) — do they have the merit and power to accomplish the ten continuous thoughts at the moment of death? If they cannot, where will they go after death, and what will be their retribution in life after life to come?

As for the people who commit the five heinous offenses and the ten evil deeds spoken of in the Contemplation Sutra of the Buddha of Immeasurable Life — why is it that at the moment of death they can meet a good spiritual friend who teaches them to recite the Buddha’s name? Why can they immediately and gladly believe and accept, and sincerely recite, accomplishing the ten continuous thoughts
? The patriarchs and great masters of the Pure Land school throughout history have given very many teachings on this matter; a single look will confirm it, so I need not elaborate here.

Q: In proclaiming “reciting the name brings certain rebirth, no need to cultivate, no need to observe the precepts, no need to do good, no need to purify one’s own mind, even doing evil for a whole life is of no consequence” — where does the seriousness of its consequences lie?

A: Proclaiming “reciting the name brings certain rebirth, no need to cultivate” is urging people to be lazy; and proclaiming “no need to observe the precepts, no need to do good, no need to purify one’s own mind, even doing evil for a whole life is of no consequence” is urging people to do evil. A person so formed is both lazy and evil; can he be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss? Since he cannot be reborn in the Western Pure Land of Ultimate Bliss, then where will he go at death? And what will be his retribution in life after life to come? This is speaking of the individual. If we speak of the Buddhist community, what kind of scene will result if this goes on? Read
“The Practice of Master Honen’s Teaching”
, and it is clear.

Teaching Dharma while violating the meaning of the scriptures, distorting the scriptural text, slandering the Buddha and destroying the Dharma — this is impure teaching. Those who teach impurely have extremely heavy offenses (more than taking the lives of all sentient beings in the three thousand great thousand worlds), a very fearful retribution (falling into the great hell), and their believers likewise come to a very miserable end (entering the wrong path from which it is hard to return, enduring manifold afflictions and endless suffering for a hundred thousand myriad eons).
The Buddha said:
“Sariputra, though a resentful enemy
(though the resentful thief is vicious and takes life)
takes away life
(but the life taken is only this one life)
, such a foolish person teaching impurely causes great affliction to sentient beings for a hundred thousand myriad eons
(because their believers, with wrong views entering the mind, life after life, for a hundred thousand myriad eons, find it hard to escape, and calamities come without cease)
. Such a person
(a person deluded by impure teaching)

is dull and deluded, covering the fundamental bodhi mind of the Buddha, and his greed and clinging blaze again, continuing without interruption; because of that greed and clinging, he wanders through the five paths, with no good road, and birth and death never cease. Therefore, Sariputra,
those who teach impurely commit exceedingly many offenses, and also act as evil spiritual friends to sentient beings, and also slander the Buddhas of the past, future, and present
. Sariputra, setting aside the sentient beings of this Jambudvipa,
if a person were to take the lives of all sentient beings in the three thousand great thousand worlds, the offense of impure teaching is greater than this
. Why? Because such people destroy the Anuttara-samyak-sambodhi of all Buddhas and aid the work of Mara,
and also cause sentient beings to endure manifold afflictions for a hundred thousand myriad eons
; they can only bind, and cannot free. Know that such a person is an evil spiritual friend to sentient beings, and speaking falsely in the great assembly slanders the Buddhas,
and because of this cause falls into the great hell
Therefore you should know,
such a person would rather cut out his tongue with a sharp knife than teach impurely in the assembly
(The Buddha’s Treasury Sutra)

[The five paths] The heavens, humans, hells, hungry ghosts, and animals. If one speaks of the six paths, the asuras are added. Here they are not mentioned because the asura path is included within the heavens, humans, animals, and hungry ghosts.
Q: Why must the Fundamental Vow Dharma be criticized?
A: Because what the Fundamental Vow Dharma does possesses the three great characteristics of
destroying the right Dharma of the Buddha
First,
inverted teaching
, replacing the right Dharma with false Dharma. Second,
instigating the breaking of precepts and the doing of evil

, corrupting the four assemblies of renunciants and laypeople, and especially wanting to destroy the true Sangha that is the field of merit and model for humans and devas, in order to destroy the right Dharma of the Buddha.
The Buddha said:
“The destruction of the right Dharma in the future lies not in the destruction by maras and non-Buddhist teachers, but precisely in the corruption and collapse of the Sangha!”
(A Discourse on the Treasure of the Sangha)
Third,
exterminating those who differ, monopolizing the world
(see the “threefold discarding and establishing” in the article
“The Fundamental Vow Dharma Is a Non-Buddhist School Attached to Buddhism”
), making the Buddhist community a world under the unified rule of false Dharma and evil people.
In this way, the right Dharma of the Buddha is destroyed. And the retribution for destroying the right Dharma of the Buddha is extremely painful

— whether it be the propagators of the Fundamental Vow Dharma, or their followers, supporters, and backers (the offenses of these three latter kinds of people are those of aiding the tiger in its evil)
, all will fall into the Avici hell for long eons
. So, whether to protect the right Dharma or out of compassion, the Fundamental Vow Dharma must be criticized,
so that everyone may know the truth

(Those who deliberately do evil need not be discussed; but those believers who, not knowing the truth, mistakenly board the pirate ship and suffer this ruinous calamity — it is truly too wretched. Oh boundless heavens, what men are these!)
